summary: Backend testing of NEW D&D world endpoints (v6_dnd_resources_001 + v6_dnd_steden_drag_001). All 18 pytest tests passed (100%): resources CRUD (admin happy path, non-admin 403, not-found 404), image upload + fetch via /api/system-archive/file/{id}, auto-creation of game-card (with class='game', kind='resource', image_urls) AND KB v2 inbox card (with begrip + 'grondstof' tag), Leeuwarden drag PATCH + admin enforcement, plus regression on existing /fracties, /provincies, /steden endpoints. Teardown restored Leeuwarden coords and deleted all TEST_-prefixed resources.
critical_code_review_comments: world.py is 597 lines — approaching split threshold (>700). Consider extracting resources sub-module (RESOURCE_TYPES + create/patch/delete handlers + helpers) into modules/dnd/world_resources.py.

POST /resources: failures in _create_game_card_for_resource or _create_kb_inbox_card_for_resource are silently swallowed (try/except: pass returns None). If KB inbox write fails the API still returns success with linked_kb_card_id=null. Consider logging via logger.warning so silent failures are observable.

DELETE /resources/{id}: docstring says 'linked card blijft staan, image blijft in archive' — by design, but this leaks orphan game/KB cards + archive files. Add a cascade option or at minimum a cleanup helper.

_save_image_to_system_archive uses uuid.uuid4().hex[:12] for file IDs — 48 bits of entropy is fine, but collisions aren't checked against SA_INDEX before writing. Cheap to add: `while any(e['id']==file_id for e in idx['files']): file_id = uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]`.
MAX_IMAGE_MB = 8 is hardcoded; consider env var. Also: image content is loaded fully into memory via await image.read() — fine for 8MB cap but worth a note for future video/larger media.
